families.hypothesis: High trailing funding marks crowded leveraged longs: they pay carry and underperform as the crowding unwinds. Low or negative funding marks crowded shorts. The other side is retail leveraged longs chasing hot alts, who are price-insensitive to the 8h fee. Arbitrage is limited because alts have no spot borrow and squeeze risk is high, so the premium persists.
families.grid: Pre-registered (42): A1 score=-(funding sum over L days), L in {1,3,7,14} x top50/top100 x quintile/rank-weighted x rebalance 1/3d = 32. A2 delta funding (3d, 7d) x top50/100 x q/r = 8. A3 funding residualised on 14d-momentum rank (q/r) = 2. Funding relative to BTC has the same cross-sectional rank as A1, so it was not run. Post-hoc, counted (10): A4 tercile (L7/L14 x rb1/3) and rank on top-30 (L7/L14) = 6. A5 funding residualised on liquidity (2). A6 short-tercile with BTC+ETH hedge or EW-universe hedge (2). Total 52.
families.summary: Persistent funding (L7/L14) works. Rank-weighted Sharpe is 1.47-1.71 across all 8 universe/rebalance combinations (a plateau); quintile gives 0.99-1.44. L1/L3 are noisy and negative in 2022-24. Delta-funding (A2) has no edge. The price part alone, net of costs, has Sharpe about 1.0-1.3, so this is not pure carry; carry adds about +10%/yr, almost all received on the short leg. Spot-return PnL equals perp-return PnL, so it is not basis convergence. The edge sits in the short leg: Sharpe 2.2 vs EW, positive every year. The long leg is about 0.6 vs EW and about 0 in 2020/2023/2024. Correlation is +0.09 with 14d XS momentum, -0.07 with BTC and +0.06 with 3d reversal. The edge survives residualising on momentum and on liquidity. 2021 dominates the return, the top-5 coins produce 53% of PnL, and the rolling 1-year Sharpe dipped to -1.45 in mid-2024.

families.family: B(i): delta-neutral cash-and-carry (long spot + short perp)
families.hypothesis: Perp longs pay a structural leverage premium. A hedged spot-long/perp-short position collects it with near-zero price risk. Selecting coins with high trailing funding should raise the yield.
families.grid: Pre-registered (19): trailing 3d/7d funding APR threshold {0,10,20,40%} on top-50 with spot available (8) and on BTC+ETH only (8). Always-on BTC+ETH (1). Top-N by 7d funding, N in {3,10} (2). Equal notional across selected coins, daily, spot 0.10% + perp 0.07% per side, basis changes included.
families.summary: Selecting high-funding coins destroys value: funding mean-reverts after entry and each switch costs 0.34% round trip. Alt and top-N versions earn -4% to +8% APR and lose in 2022 (down to -29%). The best configuration is the dumbest: always-on BTC+ETH, 16.7% CAGR on notional (about 12.3% on capital at 3x perp margin), Sharpe 9.5, MaxDD -1.7%. Yearly: 2020 +22.8%, 2021 +40.4%, 2022 +2.4%, 2023 +8.3%, 2024 +13.3%; 2021 supplied 44% of the log-return. This is a market-wide carry premium whose level depends on the leverage regime, not a selection alpha. Its tail risks (exchange, USDT, margin) are not visible in daily data.

families.hypothesis: High-funding coins dip into settlement as longs exit to avoid paying, then recover afterwards. Negative-funding coins show the mirror pattern.
families.grid: Event study, not a strategy grid: about 215k coin-settlement events in the previous-day top-50. 7 funding buckets, conditioned on the realised rate at settlement and on the strictly-known previous rate. Windows: 1h and 3h before, 1h/3h/8h after, cross-sectionally demeaned, NW t over days. Gate: build a rule only if the gross effect is at least 0.30%.
families.summary: NONE. The one large effect, +45bp in the 3h before settlement when realised funding is <= -0.05%, uses information that is only fully known at settlement. On the strictly-known previous rate it falls to +2.6bp (t -0.4). 'High funding dips then recovers' is absent: for funding >= 0.1%, the 3h before is -8bp (t -0.9) and the 1h after is +0.4bp. Every after-settlement window is under 10bp, far below the 0.14% round-trip cost. No rule was built.

candidates.name: A4_L14_top50_tercile_rb1 (funding-crowding L/S, tercile)
candidates.rationale: Short persistently crowded leveraged longs (high 14d funding) and long the crowded shorts. The position collects the carry plus the price underperformance as crowding unwinds. It is the implementable equal-weight version of the pre-registered A1_L14 rank signal.
candidates.rules: Daily at 00:00 UTC. Universe: point-in-time top-50 Binance USDT perps by trailing 30d median quote volume, at least 60 days listed. Signal: F14 = sum of the last 14 days of funding settlements (known at close). Short the top third by F14, equal weight, -0.5 gross total. Long the bottom third, equal weight, +0.5 gross total. Dollar-neutral, rebalanced daily to target. No stops; positions change only through rebalancing. Costs 0.07%/side plus actual funding.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Price per year: 12.6% / 87.9% / 16.5% / 7.9% / 14.1%. Funding per year: 10.9% / 13.8% / 9.1% / 6.3% / 7.5%. Costs about 4.5%/yr. Price part net of costs is positive every year (whole-period Sharpe about 1.1-1.3), so this is not pure carry. Funding comes almost entirely from the short leg (+11%/yr); the long leg pays -1.5%/yr. Price PnL measured on spot returns matches perp returns (0.30 vs 0.31/yr), so it is not basis convergence.
candidates.concerns: 1. 2021 alt-mania supplied more than half the log-return. 2. The rolling 1-year Sharpe bottomed at -1.45 in June 2024, so long weak stretches happen. 3. The top-5 coins (CRV, BNB, LINK, TRX, FIL, mostly long-side large caps) produce 53% of PnL; dropping them with hindsight leaves Sharpe 1.21, with 2023-24 at 0.69. 4. The long leg is close to zero vs EW after 2022; the edge is the short leg. Survivorship bias likely understates the short leg and inflates the long leg. 5. The tercile implementation is post-hoc (the pre-registered twin is A1 rank-weighted). 6. Positive skew 2.8 and kurtosis 43: a few crash months of the crowded names drive results. 7. Leg Sharpes are measured against an equal-weight universe; raw long-only is 1.25 and raw short-only -0.48. 8. These are Binance funding rates; HYPE funding is hourly with a different universe, so the signal must be rebuilt there. At $200 it needs about 1.4x gross for $10 minimum positions.
candidates.script: C:\Crypto data\backtest data and more\alpha_20261024\hunt\h1_funding\famA_deep.py (also famA_grid.py, famA_conc.py, famA_size.py, famA_checks.py, final_numbers.py, dsr_calc.py)

candidates.name: A1_L14_top50_rank_rb1 (pre-registered twin, rank-weighted)
candidates.rationale: Same crowding/carry signal, exactly as pre-registered: rank-proportional dollar-neutral weights across the whole top-50.
candidates.rules: Daily. Top-50 point-in-time liquidity universe. Score = -(14-day funding sum). Weights proportional to the cross-sectionally demeaned percentile rank of the score, |w| summing to 1, dollar-neutral. Rebalance daily. 0.07%/side plus funding.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Funding about +10.7%/yr, costs 4.1%/yr. Price part net of costs has Sharpe about 0.97 and is positive in every sub-period.
candidates.concerns: Same concerns as the tercile version, with a weaker 2024 (Sharpe 0.48). The tiny near-median weights make it untradeable at $200 (minimum equity about $12.5k for $10 positions). Its role is to confirm that the signal holds on a plateau and is not an artifact of the tercile choice.

candidates.name: A6b short high-funding tercile + equal-weight long top-50 hedge (post-hoc)
candidates.rationale: Leg decomposition showed the edge is in shorting crowded longs. This variant keeps only that leg and hedges market beta with an equal-weight long of the universe instead of the weak low-funding long leg.
candidates.rules: Daily. Top-50 universe. Short the top third by 14d funding sum, equal weight, -0.5 gross. Long all top-50 names equally, +0.5 gross. Rebalance daily. 0.07%/side plus funding.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Funding +4.4%/yr, costs 2.6%/yr. Price part net of costs has Sharpe 1.30, positive every year.
candidates.concerns: Chosen post-hoc after seeing the leg split, so it is not independent of A4; treat it as the same signal. The BTC+ETH-hedged version (A6a) fails (Sharpe 0.46, 2021 -19%), so the hedge has to be an alt basket, which needs about 39 positions (about $1k minimum). There is no plateau check for this variant.

candidates.name: A2_d7_top100_q (change in funding), best 'none' of the delta variants
candidates.rationale: A rising funding rate should flag new crowding before the level does.
candidates.rules: Daily. Score = -(F7(t) - F7(t-7)). Top-100. Quintile L/S equal weight. Rebalance daily.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Price part net of costs has Sharpe 0.55, entirely from 2020-21. The 3d delta is negative (-0.6).
candidates.concerns: Negative or flat after 2021. High turnover (cost about 13%/yr). The change in funding carries no information beyond the level.

candidates.name: B3 always-on BTC+ETH cash-and-carry (long spot, short perp)
candidates.rationale: Collects the structural perp leverage premium with no price exposure. This is a risk premium, not selection alpha.
candidates.rules: Hold 50/50 BTC and ETH: long Binance spot and short an equal notional of the USDT perp. Hold continuously and keep the hedge 1:1. Costs: spot 0.10% plus perp 0.07% per side. Returns are on spot notional; capital is about 1.33x notional with the perp at 3x margin.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: About 100% funding (+15.8%/yr); basis changes -0.3%/yr; costs negligible.
candidates.concerns: Not a new alpha: a well-known market-wide carry whose level depends on the leverage regime (2022 +2.4%; the forward level is unknown). The Sharpe of 9 understates tail risks: exchange or custody failure, USDT depeg, perp margin calls in sharp rallies if spot and perp sit on separate accounts, and funding turning negative. Every selective variant (thresholds, alts, top-N) did worse than always-on, so the 'harvest high funding' hypothesis itself failed. Best used as a cash-yield sleeve under the directional strategies.

candidates.name: B1_top50_L7_thr20 (selective high-funding carry), best 'none' of the selective versions
candidates.rationale: Carry only on coins whose 7d funding exceeds 20% APR.
candidates.rules: Daily. Top-50 coins with spot available and trailing 7d funding APR > 20%: equal-notional long spot and short perp; otherwise cash. Spot 0.10% plus perp 0.07% per side.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Funding +15.2%/yr gross while invested (only 37% of the time); costs 7.7%/yr eat half of it; basis +0.4%/yr.
candidates.concerns: Returns come only from 2020-21; 2023-24 is about flat. Funding mean-reverts after selection and the entry/exit costs (0.34% round trip) eat the carry. Dominated by always-on BTC+ETH.

candidates.name: Settlement-timing event study (best attempt: post-settlement drift after strictly-known extreme funding)
candidates.rationale: Longs exit before paying high funding and re-enter after, or shorts do the mirror around negative funding.
candidates.rules: No rule built. Gate: gross per-trade effect >= 0.30%.
candidates.sample: 2020-01 to 2024-12, 1h bars, about 215k settlement events in the top-50
candidates.subperiod_sharpe: n/a. For realised funding >= 0.05%, the 3h-before effect by year is +0.6 / -7.9 / -3.8 / +3.7 bp (2020/21/23/24), with no stable sign.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: n/a
candidates.concerns: The only large effect (+45bp in the 3h before settlement when realised funding <= -0.05%, t 7.6) relies on the realised rate, which is only fully known at settlement; it is the squeeze itself. On the previous, known rate it is +2.6bp (t -0.4). Every after-settlement window is under 10bp, below the 0.14% round-trip cost.

families.hypothesis: Pre-registered: retail account crowding (global_ls) is contrarian; the top-trader position tilt (top_pos_ls) is informed. Retail longs supply liquidity to informed flow. Ratio levels differ per coin, so transform per coin first and then rank cross-sectionally.
families.grid: Pre-registered 15: -tsz(G,30/90), tsz(T,30/90), tsz(T)-tsz(G) 30/90, -dlogG 1/3/7, dlogT-dlogG 1/3/7, tsz(log Tpos/Tacct) 30/90, -log G level. Robustness 8 (reb3, top100, q33, mom-neutral on the best 2). 1 sign flip. 2 size/mom-neutral. A7 refinement 8 (smoothing 7/14 x rebalance 1/3/7, raw reb7, top100). 1 mom-neutral. Level tests 3 (Tpos-G, Tacct-G, Tpos). Post-hoc 3 (-Tpos level, consensus, fund-neutral). A9f neighbours 4 + top100 1. Blend 1. Universe top-50 PIT, quintile L/S, cost 0.07% + funding.
families.summary: Time-series z-scores and changes of all ratios fail: Sharpe -1.95 to +0.51, all negative at 2x cost. 1d changes are mostly short-term reversal and are killed by turnover. The 'top traders are informed' idea is rejected and in fact reversed: the level of top_pos_ls has Sharpe -1.54. Levels work when traded as crowding contrarian. A7 (-mean14 log global_ls, pre-registered direction) scores 1.06 but is weak: t 1.76, a third is momentum, 2024 is fading. A9f (-mean14 log top_pos_ls, post-hoc flip) scores 1.33 over 2021-12 to 2024 and 1.74 over 2023-24, with spanning alpha vs funding t 2.54. The 50/50 blend scores 1.52. Effective sample 2022-24 for global_ls and only 2023-24 for top-trader fields.

families.hypothesis: OI growth is crowding and should be faded. Price-down with OI-up is squeeze fuel; price-up with OI-down is a weak short-covering rally. A high OI/ADV leverage ratio is crowded. Taker-buy imbalance is impatient flow that reverts. Also check whether each is repackaged funding.
families.grid: Pre-registered 21: -dOI 1/3/7; rank(dOI)-rank(ret) 1/3/7; -ret 1/3/7 controls; discrete quadrants 3/7; -log(OI/ADV30) level, -tsz90, -dlev7; -imb_k raw 1/3/7 and ts-demeaned 1/3/7 (kline tbqv/qv, 2020+); -tsz(taker_ls_vol,30). Robustness 8 (reb3, top100, q33, fund-neutral on B3 -dlev7 and -zlev90). Post-hoc 6: +imb 1/3/7, +imbdm7, mom-neutral +imb 3/7. The optional 4h step was skipped because every fast signal failed at 1d.
families.summary: None. The contrarian OI, flow and reversal signals have a positive rank IC (t 4-7) but lose money as quintile L/S. The shorted winners and OI-builders have the lowest median return but the highest mean, because their right tail is fat (p99 about +25%/day). The squeeze-fuel signals and quadrants are worse than plain reversal. The best was B3 -dlev7: 0.70, or 0.82 with a 3-day rebalance. It fails 2x cost, has neighbour median 0.36, is negative in 2023, and falls to 0.14 when fund-neutral. The taker-imbalance continuation flip scores 1.16 but has correlation 0.58 with XS momentum, and the momentum-neutral version is negative: repackaged momentum. The B signals are not funding: cross-sectional correlation |c| < 0.1, imbalance about 0.2.

candidates.name: A9f_top_trader_crowding_contrarian
candidates.rationale: Large-margin Binance accounts heavily net long (high top_pos_ls) are crowded, levered, funding-paying longs. Perp demand exceeds supply, and those coins underperform as the longs unwind. Arbitrageurs and market makers are on the other side. It persists because of capacity limits, shorting frictions in alts, and the fact that the data is noisy and only covers 30 days live. The signal is aligned with funding (cross-sectional correlation 0.53 with the 30d funding level), but it is not spanned by funding factors.
candidates.rules: score_t = -mean over the trailing 14 days of log(top_pos_ls) (Binance top-trader long/short position ratio, 1d as-of close). Universe = lab.universe('1d', top_k=50, min_hist 60d). Long the top quintile and short the bottom quintile, equal weight, dollar-neutral, gross 1x. Rebalance daily at the 00:00 UTC close. Flat if fewer than 20 names have a valid score. No other exits.
candidates.sample: 2021-12-07 to 2024-12-31. Effective 2023-01 to 2024-12: 731 active days, plus 25 days in Dec-2021 and 46 in 2022.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: 2023: gross price +24.2%, funding +5.6%, cost -2.6%. 2024: +26.9%, +5.0%, -3.1%. The short leg carries it: short-leg excess vs the EW universe is +41.9%/yr (Sharpe 2.15), long-leg excess +5.0%/yr (0.25). The raw leg Sharpes in the fields include market beta.
candidates.concerns: POST-HOC SIGN FLIP: the pre-registered direction ('top traders are informed') failed with Sharpe -1.54, and the direction was flipped after seeing that. Only 2 real years. The Dec-2021 fragment lost 10%. Returns are lumpy: 2024Q4 made +31%, 2024H1 was negative. The cross-sectional correlation with the 30d funding level is 0.53. Fund7-neutral it scores 0.81. In the spanning regression on the fund7/fund30 L/S factors, alpha is +26.6%/yr (NW-t 2.54) and beta to fund30 is 0.32. Neighbour plateau: S1 0.24, S7 0.99, S30 1.19, weekly rebalance 1.22, top100 1.37. Dropping the top-10 contributors leaves 0.83; leave-one-out minimum is 1.15. DSR is 0.57 at n=82. Survivorship: the short-leg-driven PnL is understated by the bias, which is good here. Hyperliquid coverage of these 50 names was not checked.

candidates.name: BLEND_positioning_crowding_contrarian_A7_A9f_50_50
candidates.rationale: One hypothesis, crowded long positioning is contrarian, measured two ways: by account count (retail global_ls) and by top-trader position size (top_pos_ls). The two components correlate 0.26 in 2023-24, so blending improves the Sharpe and halves the drawdown.
candidates.rules: W = 0.5 * W_A7 + 0.5 * W_A9f. W_A7 = quintile L/S on -mean_14d(log global_ls). W_A9f = quintile L/S on -mean_14d(log top_pos_ls). Both use top-50 PIT, equal weight, dollar-neutral, gross 1x each before the 0.5 scaling. Rebalance daily at 00:00 UTC, flat if fewer than 20 names. Drop any position worth less than $10.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Gross price about +20%/yr, funding +2.4%/yr, cost -2.5%/yr
candidates.concerns: The blend is post-hoc and inherits A9f's post-hoc sign and its 2-year sample. Because the two books net against each other, some positions become tiny: the median minimum is about $3.6k by formula, and about $400 is realistic once positions under $10 are dropped. Do not re-tune the smoothing. Freeze it as written. Its DSR is 0.69 at n=82, with the selection inside the blend acknowledged.

candidates.name: A7_S14_retail_account_crowding_contrarian
candidates.rationale: Retail accounts buy dips and short rallies. Coins with many retail accounts net long relative to short (high global_ls) are bag-holder coins that keep lagging, and coins retail is shorting tend to squeeze. The pre-registered direction held.
candidates.rules: score_t = -mean over the trailing 14 days of log(global_ls). Top-50 PIT universe, quintile L/S, equal weight, dollar-neutral, gross 1x. Rebalance daily at 00:00 UTC. Flat if fewer than 20 names.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Almost all price: gross +16-39%/yr, funding about +1%/yr, cost -3%/yr. Both legs add: long-leg excess +27.9%/yr (Sharpe 1.10), short-leg excess +20.8%/yr (0.91).
candidates.concerns: t_NW is 1.76 and DSR 0.38-0.45. The cross-sectional correlation with 60d return is 0.43, and the momentum-neutral version scores only 0.56 (2023 -0.30). The effect decays through 2024 (0.59). Returns are lumpy: 2022Q4 +25% and 2023Q2 +20%. Dropping the top-10 contributors leaves 0.65. The plateau across smoothing/rebalance cells is 0.59-1.13; top100 gives 1.28. It is not size (size-neutral 0.70) and not funding (correlation 0.01). Survivorship inflates the long leg.

candidates.name: A6_zTpos_over_acct_30 (best ts-z/change attempt, family A)
candidates.rationale: When the largest top traders (position-weighted) are more long than the average top account, that should be informed size.
candidates.rules: score = tsz(log(top_pos_ls/top_acct_ls), 30d trailing). Top-50 PIT universe, quintile L/S, daily rebalance.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Gross +22%/yr, eaten by 14%/yr of cost
candidates.concerns: This is the best of 10 time-series z-score and change configs; all of them are negative at 2x cost. The momentum-neutral version scores -0.39.

candidates.name: B3_-dlev7_reb3 (best OI attempt, family B)
candidates.rationale: When OI falls relative to trading volume, leverage is being flushed and the coin is less crowded, so go long. When leverage builds, go short.
candidates.rules: score = -(log(OI/ADV30)_t - log(OI/ADV30)_{t-7}). Top-50 PIT universe, quintile L/S, rebalanced every 3 days.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Gross price +26%/yr, cost -9%/yr, funding about 0
candidates.concerns: The daily-rebalance base is 0.70 and fails 2x cost (-0.12). Top100 gives 0.41, q33 0.31, fund-neutral 0.14. 2023 is negative. Every other OI signal (dOI, squeeze fuel, quadrants) has Sharpe between -1 and -2.6, because the short leg's fat right tail kills the rank-IC edge.

candidates.name: B4f_imb7_taker_buy_continuation (post-hoc flip, family B)
candidates.rationale: Aggressive taker buying is informed or persistent demand with permanent impact, so it should continue. This is the flip of the pre-registered contrarian test, which was negative every year.
candidates.rules: score = sum_7d tbqv / sum_7d qv (kline taker-buy share). Top-50 PIT universe, quintile L/S, daily rebalance.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Gross +37%/yr, cost -10%, funding +4%
candidates.concerns: Repackaged XS momentum: correlation 0.58 with 14d XS momentum, the same 2023 drawdown pattern, and the momentum-neutral versions are negative (imb7 -0.21, imb3 -0.66). Neighbours: imb3 0.71, imbdm7 0.58, imb1 -0.49. The long leg is survivorship-inflated.

families.hypothesis: Liquidity-demanding flow (liquidations, retail market orders) pushes prices away from value, and the liquidity provider earns the reversion. Low-abnormal-volume moves should revert (no information). High-abnormal-volume moves should continue (CGW 1993, Llorente et al. 2002). Residual returns vs BTC beta should isolate the idiosyncratic, liquidity-driven part.
families.grid: Pre-registered, 40 configs. A1 1d: L in {1,2,3,5} days x {RAW, RESID vs 60d BTC beta} x {fresh daily book, 3-day overlapping books} = 16. A2 1d: L in {1,3} x {RAW, RESID} x {low, high abnormal-volume half; q=0.3 inside the half} = 8. A3 4h: h in {1,3,6} bars x {RAW, RESID} x {every bar, 6-bar overlapping} = 12. A4 4h: h in {3,6} x RAW x {low, high AV half} = 4. All use quintile $-neutral books on the top-50 point-in-time universe. Post-hoc A-flip (ex-post sign flip, 4 configs): 3d residual or raw momentum, including inside the high-AV half. Effective trials for DSR = 84.
families.summary: NONE. 1d: no reversal at any horizon. The cross-section shows continuation: gross Sharpe of the reversal book is -0.4 to -1.4, net -1.2 to -2.2. High-volume moves continue strongly, but low-volume moves do not revert either. 4h: a real gross liquidity-provision premium exists. A3 h1 RAW: gross +31%/yr, Sharpe 1.01. A4 h3 low-AV: gross Sharpe 1.14, while high-AV continues at -1.32, which matches the volume hypothesis. But turnover is about 2,200-3,400x per year, cost drag 157-236%/yr, and break-even cost about 0.9bp per side. The signal dies within one bar. Only a sub-bar maker with rebates could harvest it. The flipped 1-5d momentum (A-flip) has gross Sharpe about 1.0 and net 0.3-0.5, but 2022 is about -2, 2x-cost Sharpe is at most 0, corr with xsmom14 is 0.38-0.57, and spanning alpha after xsmom14 is -2% to -6%/yr. It is the existing momentum factor.

families.family: B low-risk & lottery anomalies (BAB, IVOL, MAX, skewness)
families.hypothesis: Leverage-constrained, lottery-seeking retail traders overpay for high-beta, high-IVOL, high-MAX, positively skewed coins. The trade is long boring coins, short lottery coins. BAB: long low-beta levered to beta, short high-beta delevered.
families.grid: Pre-registered, 36 configs, 1d, top-50 ex BTC, q=0.2. BAB beta {60,90}d. IVOL residual vol {30,60}d. MAX1 and MAX5 over 30d. SKEW daily {30,90}d and 4h-return skew over 30d. Each x {DN $-neutral quintiles, BN beta-neutral FP-style legs (shrunk 60d beta, leg beta 0.5, leg gross cap 1)} x {daily, weekly}. Post-hoc B-rev (ex-post sign flip, 'lottery premium'): 10 configs + 3 robustness (top30, top100, q=0.3). Plus 1 post-hoc short-leg-only BTC-hedged config. Effective trials for DSR = 86.
families.summary: Textbook direction REJECTED in 28/28 IVOL/MAX/SKEW configs (net Sharpe -1.32 to 0.00). Lottery-like coins outperformed in 2020-24. Boring coins won only in the 2022 bear market (IVOL DN 2022: +1.4 to +2.0). BAB DN is negative. Only BAB-BN is positive: best 0.83, but 2023-24 is -0.70, and SOL/AVAX/EGLD/AAVE/FIL in 2021 give 125% of all price PnL, a survivorship-flattered long leg. Weak. The sign-flipped lottery premium (long positive-skew, short negative-skew 4h-return coins) has net Sharpe 0.86, 0.67 at 2x cost, 1.00 at lag 1, and plateau median 0.78. But 2022 is -0.41, spanning alpha after BTC + xsmom14 + 3d momentum is +9%/yr (t 0.66), and DSR is 0.19. Weak. The PnL comes from the short leg (negative-skew coins lag the EW universe in every year). That leg alone with a BTC hedge fails (Sharpe 0.14, 2021 -52%). Survivorship biases the textbook short leg against the anomaly, but the rejection is too broad for it to matter. It flatters the BAB-BN and B-rev long legs.

candidates.name: B_BAB_b90_BN_R7
candidates.rationale: Frazzini-Pedersen betting-against-beta: leverage-constrained traders bid up high-beta coins. Built beta-neutral, so it is not a disguised short-beta bet.
candidates.rules: Universe: lab.universe('1d', min_hist_days=60, top_k=50) excluding BTC. Signal: -beta of daily returns vs BTC over a 90d trailing OLS. Long the bottom-beta quintile, short the top-beta quintile, equal weight inside each leg. Each leg is scaled so its shrunk beta (0.6*OLS60 + 0.4*XS median) = 0.5, with leg gross capped at 1.0. families.hypothesis: A rich perp premium or basis means levered longs are paying up (retail leverage demand), so those coins should underperform. A discount means hedging or short pressure, so those coins should rebound. It persists because arbitrage is limited: cash-and-carry needs capital on both legs and reverse carry needs a scarce alt spot borrow. Funding is clamped at 0.01%/8h inside a band, so prem_mean might carry information beyond funding.
families.grid: Pre-registered in the header of 10_basis_premium.py. Universe top-50, quintile L/S, daily rebalance, contrarian sign. A1 prem_mean level L=1/3/7/14. A2 prem_mean trailing-90d z L=1/3/7. A3 basis (perp close/Binance spot close-1) level L=1/3/7. A4 basis z L=3/7. A5 premium-minus-funding rank L=3/7. A6 demean weights x2. A7 rebalance every 3 days x2. A0 funding control (-fund_7). Plus 10 robustness configs in 30_basis_deepdive.py: premium snapshot, basis minus premium, skip-today, top-30, top-80, L=14. Plus 1 declared post-hoc combo C1.
families.summary: prem_mean contrarian is essentially the trailing-funding factor: XS Spearman 0.81 with fund_7, return correlation 0.79. Sharpe is about 1.1, but it is all 2020-21; 2023-24 is negative. The premium-beyond-funding configs (A5) lose -1.2 to -1.3, so prem_mean adds nothing beyond funding. The spot-perp BASIS 7d level is different: Sharpe 1.21, positive in every sub-period and every year, 2x cost 0.77, lag1 0.80, plateau median 1.07, return correlation 0.36 with the funding control. With the same weights, PnL on spot prices is still Sharpe 1.04 (0.92 with a 1-bar delay), so it is not a perp close-bounce artifact. Neither decomposed component works alone: the premium snapshot is 2020-21 heavy and Binance spot vs index has no edge. DSR is only 0.50 at n=73. Best: A3_basis_lvl_7 (promising); alternate A4_basis_z_7.

families.hypothesis: Taker-buy ratio: informed takers predict continuation, while absorbed levered noise predicts reversal. Flow-price divergence (heavy taker buying with a flat price) means passive sellers are absorbing, so the price should fall.

candidates.name: A3_basis_lvl_7
candidates.rationale: The Binance perp-vs-spot basis reflects whether the marginal demand in a coin comes from perp leverage or from spot. When the perp is rich, levered longs are crowded; they pay funding and then underperform. When the perp is at a discount, short or hedging pressure that arbs cannot close (scarce alt spot borrow for reverse carry) tends to unwind. The signal adds beyond funding: XS Spearman with fund_7 is only 0.40, and the edge shows up in spot-price PnL too.
candidates.rules: Signal: basis = perp close / Binance spot close - 1 at the daily 00:00 UTC close; set NaN if |basis| >= 5%; s = 7-day rolling mean (min_periods 4); score = -s. Universe: lab.universe('1d', min_hist_days=60, top_k=50), restricted to coins with a spot close that day. Weights: lab.quantile_ls_weights(score, U, q=0.2), i.e. long the lowest-basis quintile and short the highest, equal weight, dollar neutral, gross 1.0. Rebalance daily at the close. No stops; exits only through rank changes.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Gross price +34.6%/yr, funding received +8.2%/yr, cost drag -11.4%/yr. With the same weights, spot-price PnL is +26.9%/yr (Sharpe 1.04), versus +34.4% on perp prices, so about 7%/yr is basis convergence. Excess over the EW basket: long leg Sharpe 0.78, short leg 1.25. Raw leg Sharpes are long 1.17 / short -0.49.
candidates.concerns: Weak statistical significance: DSR is 0.50 at n=73 (0.72 at an effective n=20), and regression alpha versus BTC, XS-mom and the funding factor is +19.6%/yr with t_NW only 1.87. PnL is concentrated: CRV, BNB, ETC, DOGE and ETH are 83% of gross, and dropping the top 3 coins gives Sharpe 0.84. Dropping today's snapshot (skip-today) cuts Sharpe to 0.80, so it depends on the fresh 00:00 UTC reading, which is also the funding timestamp and a thin-liquidity moment. Neighbour L=14 is only 0.64. The 2020 universe is small (about 14 coins). The signal needs Binance spot and perp data; it is untested on Hyperliquid fees, hourly funding and its coin list. $200 is just at the $10-per-position minimum. Survivorship is less of a worry because most of the excess comes from the short leg.

A2 1h: windows {Asia 00-07, Europe 08-12, US-open 13-15, US 13-20, pre-funding hours 07/15/23, post-funding hours 00/08/16, top-3 |t| hours}, direction = sign of the 2020-22 mean, plus W8 funding-conditional pre-settlement (hold -sign(last 8h funding) when |f| >= 0.03%), x {BTC, ETH, EW20} = 24. A3 1h: weekend return (Fri 21:00 to Sun 22:00 UTC), hold the reversal for 24h, thr {0, 1 sd of trailing 26 weekends} x 3 assets = 6. Total 39.
families.summary: None. Weekday means are only partly persistent: Mon and Wed are positive in both halves for BTC and ETH (Spearman of weekday means 0.46-0.57), but timing rules lose to buy-and-hold: BTC Mon+Wed Sharpe 0.82 vs B&H 0.90, lag-1 -0.39. The hour-of-day profile does not persist: EST-vs-VAL correlation is -0.06 (BTC), -0.23 (ETH), -0.14 (EW20), and US-open hours flipped from positive in 2020-22 to negative in 2023-24. Gross edge is 0.3-4 bps per held hour against a 14 bps round trip, so every window rule nets Sharpe -0.25 to -7. The funding-conditional pre-settlement short makes about 8 bps per trade (price + funding) against 14 bps of cost. The weekend move has about zero correlation with the next 24h; all reversal configs are negative.

families.hypothesis: BTC leads price discovery and stale alt liquidity makes the alt basket follow BTC's last 1h/4h move, beyond the alts' own lag.

Trading: tf {1h, 4h} x form {directional alt basket = sign(z_BTC); hedged alt minus beta*BTC on the catch-up gap z} x k {0.5, 1, 2} x hold {1, 3 bars} = 24, plus cross-sectional beta catch-up (w_i ~ demeaned beta_i*r_BTC - r_i) at tf {1h, 4h} x L {1, 3} = 4. Total 28.
families.summary: None, and the sign is the opposite of the hypothesis. Next-bar alt basket return on BTC's last bar, controlling for the alts' own lag: -0.074 (HAC t -2.4) at 4h, -0.066 (t -3.4) at 1h. BTC also reverses its own last bar (t about -2 to -3). Every directional and hedged rule loses; the best is 4h D k2 h3 at Sharpe -0.10. The 1h cross-sectional residual reversal has gross Sharpe 4.6 but 12,700x/yr turnover (cost 887%/yr), so it is microstructure that only a maker can harvest.

families.hypothesis: Fast BTC drops are liquidation and stop cascades that overshoot. Liquidity providers are paid by the next-bar bounce, and the more levered alts bounce more (Nagel-style reversal as a return to liquidity provision).
families.grid: Long EW top-20 ex-BTC alt basket for h 4h-bars after a trigger: {down: z_BTC < -k; abs: |z_BTC| > k} x k {1.5, 2, 2.5} x h {1, 3, 6} = 18 configs. Deflated Sharpe counts 46 trials (B1 + B1R) because the idea came from B1's descriptive result.
families.summary: Weak. All 18 configs are positive (Sharpe 0.15-0.94, median about 0.7), but none reaches 1.0. Hold-1 versions (0.72-0.91) fail lag-1 because the bounce is over within 4h. The h6 versions survive lag-1 but are mostly 2021 alt-season beta (corr BTC 0.5-0.6). Alpha vs alt buy-and-hold has t of 1.1-1.6, deflated-Sharpe probability 0.2-0.35, and the top 10% of bars give more than 100% of gross PnL. Survivorship flatters it a lot (dead coins were exactly the failed dip-buys), and it overlaps CLR's liquidation-flush long.

families.hypothesis: Realised vol is persistent but does not forecast returns proportionally, so 1/sigma scaling (Moreira-Muir) or drawdown control raises the risk-adjusted return of long-crypto exposure and cuts crash tails.

families.summary: None. Alpha vs same-asset buy-and-hold has |t| < 1.1 for every pure vol-scaling config, and Sharpe moves about ±0.1 around B&H (BTC B&H 0.87, EW20 0.74-0.83). Every config is negative in 2022, and the 4h EW20 versions are worse (alpha t down to -2.2). The best number, BTC drawdown-20% filter at Sharpe 1.11, is a trend filter (RNT territory): flat in 2022, -18% in 2021, neighbours 0.96 and 0.80. Long perp exposure paid about 10-12%/yr in funding over 2020-24.

candidates.name: B1R 4h shockrev down k2.5 h1
candidates.rationale: BTC 4h crashes of more than 2.5 sigma are forced-liquidation flow. Absorbing it in the levered alt basket earns the overshoot bounce over the next 4h. The other side is liquidated longs and stop cascades, and it persists because liquidity provision is capital-constrained in stress.
candidates.rules: Universe: equal-weight top-20 Binance perps by trailing-30d median quote volume (lab.universe 1d, top_k 20, min_hist 60d), excluding BTC, mapped to 4h without lookahead. Signal: z = BTC 4h return / trailing 30d (180-bar) std of BTC 4h returns. Entry: at the close of any 4h bar with z < -2.5, go long the EW alt basket at 1x gross. Exit: at the next 4h close; a new trigger extends the hold by one bar. Otherwise flat. Long only.
candidates.price_vs_funding_split: Price +24.7%/yr, funding +0.1%/yr, costs -4.5%/yr. Long only, in the market 1.5% of the time (164 events). avg_n_pos is the average while in the market; time-averaged it is 0.27.
candidates.concerns: The rule came from data: B1's lead-lag sign was the reverse of the hypothesis. It fails lag-1 badly (-0.81) because the bounce is over within one 4h bar; the 1h event study shows the bounce spread over hours 1-4, so minutes of delay are fine but a bar is not. Only 164 events, daily kurtosis 173, top-10% bars make more than 100% of gross PnL, calendar 2020 was -13%, and 2022 was only 0.24. Alpha vs alt buy-and-hold is +18%/yr but t is only 1.62. Survivorship strongly flatters it: it buys alt dips, and coins whose dips never recovered (LUNA, FTT) are not in the alive-in-2026 universe. It overlaps CLR's 4h liquidation-flush basket long. IS from $200 ends at $477 (low $152). Needs about 18 alts x $10, i.e. $190 minimum at 1x. Below the forwarding bar (Sharpe < 1, lag-1 < 0.6).
